annotations.text:
SPOTLIGHT — what's built today.
Axis: the room goes dark so Ria is the only thing you can look at. Four cards, each pointing at one control.
For: nothing competes with it, and the card and the thing it names are on screen together.
Tradeoff: the app is inert while it runs — you read about a control you can't touch — and it is four interruptions before you start.

RIA'S VOICE — no overlay at all.
Axis: the tutorial isn't a layer over the product, it IS the product. Her footer slab grows to hold what she's saying, and the part she's naming is tinted in that same slab colour.
For: nothing is blocked, so you can try each thing as you read it. No new surface to design or dismiss.
Tradeoff: quiet. On a busy call it can be missed, and it displaces her own footer while it runs.

ONE-PAGER — read once, dismiss once.
Axis: no stepping. One sheet with the panel drawn small and its four parts numbered.
For: fifteen seconds, one decision, no pointer-chasing. Easy to re-open from the menu and re-read whole.
Tradeoff: the words sit beside a PICTURE of the control, not the control — you still have to find the real one afterwards.
All three carry the settled copy so you're judging the treatment, not the words.
